scores.evidence: Output filters that strip URLs, images, and @mentions from agent comments, which closes GitHub's image-render exfiltration path.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (10 s webhook timeout, HMAC, delivery-ID idempotency, metadata service blocking, CODEOWNERS/branch protection) are accurate; minor doubts such as 'Contents write on agent/* only' (GitHub Apps can't scope by branch, enforced by executor instead) and reconciling the 15-min poll stop it reaching 4.

scores.evidence: triages each issue (labels, duplicates, owner suggestion), and for eligible issues produces a draft pull request that a human reviews and merges.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolution with explicit deferrals and reasons, but the first scope is narrowed to one internal repo and the issue-status handling (closing, asking for details) is thin.

scores.evidence: An out-of-model tool executor applies writes. A human merges every PR.
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear executor, sandbox, orchestrator and Postgres roles and honored decisions; minor loose ends such as the kill switch described as emptying the allow-list versus per-repo switch.

scores.evidence: 0 escapes across ≥150 cases (ASSUMPTION: 5 channels × 6 attack goals × ≥5 variants). Permission tests: 0 successes (by design, not by filtering).
scores.rationale: Validation gates are tied to specific risks, run early before commitments, and have labeled or baseline-measured thresholds, and later phases include monitoring and drift alerts.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: issues/day per repo. Owner: repo owners, or a GitHub API history export by us.
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are labeled with owners, what they affect, and fallback if wrong (self-host flip, suggest-only).

scores.evidence: A crafted issue, comment, or linked file hijacks the agent. It then exfiltrates secrets or code, or lands malicious code in the repo.
scores.rationale: Major failure modes (injection, exfiltration, sandbox escape, runaway, missed webhooks, workflow PR) are covered with concrete handling, but issue edits during work, duplicate PRs and human collisions are not handled.

scores.evidence: Redeploy the previous image, plus a kill-switch flag (empty the repo allow-list) that stops all agent activity within one minute.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, metrics, alerts, kill switch and business-hours on-call are concrete; incident ownership and schema migration are thin.

scores.evidence: Skeleton caps: $0.25/run, $20/day. Triage ≤ $0.10/issue. Resolution attempt ≤ $5 hard cap.
scores.rationale: Caps are concrete and labeled as placeholders, with per-accepted-PR cost tracked and routing and build-vs-buy noted; there is no cost estimate from volume and sandbox or people costs are barely mentioned.

scores.evidence: Data-privacy boundary: hosted model vs self-host | R3 (source code and issue text sent out can't be recalled; contractual)
scores.rationale: Decisions are rated by reversibility, R3 ones are validated early with explicit exit paths, and the provider abstraction and deferrals are isolated.

scores.evidence: Orchestration kept to a single agent loop, every step traced, failures surfaced rather than swallowed.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with single-agent and deferred items, though the six-phase structure, nine AI sublayers and ceremony are somewhat heavy.

scores.evidence: Exit check (V0): A real issue yields a comment with one trace across every tier. A deploy and a rollback succeed through the pipeline
scores.rationale: Dependency-ordered phases with concrete tasks, checkable exits and fallbacks on failure, and the next step is specified.

checklist.evidence: Autonomous merge or auto-close of issues: pulled forward only by a new gate with a named approver
The GitHub App has minimal permissions... It has no workflows, admin, or merge permission. The agent cannot approve PRs. The model never holds a token.
All issue text, comments, linked files, and tool output are tagged as untrusted data.
Ephemeral microVM or gVisor container per run. Read-only repo snapshot... No credentials. Egress only via an allow-listed proxy
Executor pushes to agent/* and opens a draft PR... CI on agent branches runs with no secrets.
Run on ≥200 maintainer-labeled historic issues... Duplicate suggestions precision ≥ 90%
PR outcome and cost-per-PR metrics. Alerts on policy violations.
Caps on tokens, iterations, per-run cost, per-repo daily spend, and timeouts... kill-switch flag (empty the repo allow-list)
Skeleton caps: $0.25/run, $20/day. Triage ≤ $0.10/issue. Resolution attempt ≤ $5 hard cap.
Audit log of every write and approval.
ripgrep at a pinned commit SHA for code, plus an embedding index for duplicate issues
at-least-once webhooks, idempotent on delivery ID, GitHub as system of record

traps.evidence: The agent cannot merge, so there is no irreversible step.
Zero credentials inside. Egress proxy allow-list.
issue text passed as delimited data, never as instructions
Accepted-PR share ≥ UNKNOWN (product owner sets it before Phase 4).
A runaway loop is cut off at the cap and emits a cost metric.

note: Strong, safety-first and validation-driven plan with well-labeled assumptions and reversibility analysis. Weaker on human-collision and claim handling, in-flight issue edits, and audit detail for model I/O.
